34 of 100 copies appear to share flanking sequence, which would put them inside another repeat or a duplication - but this set has no 400 bp flank-decay data, and over the ~50-70 bp actually present that reading is not reliable: adjacent context and true nesting look identical at this width. Uniqueness is scored as neutral rather than penalised, and this is reported as an unmade measurement, not as evidence against the family. Re-run with 400 bp flanks to settle it.

Supported copies split into structurally different groups of 27 and 28 (within-group identity 0.72, between 0.68, excess over a random split 0.032). Both are SINEs - this does not affect the verdict, but the copies can be split if the subfamilies are wanted separately.

Separate them and re-run the whole analysis on each - the score below is withheld, because scoring a mixture answers neither question.

The copies support consensus positions 250-310 (identity 0.88) much better than the consensus as a whole (0.60). Coverage is even across the full length, so the copies are present at the ends and simply do not match there - the consensus is longer than the element it describes. Trim it to that window and re-run; the family is real, the boundary is not.
